subject: Archaeology
title: Hatshepsut: The Pharaoh They Tried to Erase
description: A quick, practical guide to Hatshepsut: The Pharaoh They Tried to Erase.

hook.text: A woman ruled Egypt as pharaoh for 20 years. After her death, someone tried to erase her from history.

buildup.text: Hatshepsut wore the false beard and royal regalia. She built Egypt's most beautiful temple at Deir el-Bahari.

discovery.text: She launched a massive trade expedition to Punt, bringing back gold, incense, and living myrrh trees.

twist.text: After her death, her stepson Thutmose III destroyed her statues and chiseled her name off monuments.

climax.text: Archaeologists pieced her story back together from fragments. Her temple still stands 3,500 years later.

punchline.text: They smashed her name off every wall. She outlasted them all.

quiz.question: Why were Hatshepsut's images and name destroyed after her death?
options: Egypt was invaded and all royal monuments were destroyed
Her stepson Thutmose III tried to erase her from history
A religious reform banned images of all previous pharaohs

details.summary: Hatshepsut was one of ancient Egypt's most successful pharaohs, ruling for over twenty years during the 18th Dynasty. She built the magnificent temple at Deir el-Bahri and expanded trade to Punt, but her successor Thutmose III later defaced her monuments.
details.whyItMatters: Hatshepsut challenges assumptions about gender in the ancient world. Her successful two-decade reign and the subsequent erasure of her memory reveal how political power and historical memory intersect.
takeaways: Hatshepsut ruled Egypt successfully for over twenty years
She built the temple at Deir el-Bahri and traded with Punt
Thutmose III later defaced her monuments and images

faq.question: Why did Thutmose III try to erase Hatshepsut?
faq.answer: Scholars debate whether it was personal hatred or political necessity. The erasure began late in Thutmose III's reign, suggesting he was securing his son's succession by removing a precedent for female rule that might complicate dynastic legitimacy.

faq.question: How did Hatshepsut legitimize herself as pharaoh?
faq.answer: She claimed divine birth from the god Amun, wore the traditional pharaonic false beard, and used kingly titles. Her propaganda emphasized divine approval rather than gender, and she maintained power through alliances with powerful officials like Senenmut.
